newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forex market dull on lack of demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forex market dull on lack of demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee was steady against the dollar on Thursday, due to a lack of commercial demand for the greenback, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was quoted at its opening level of 58.45 to the dollar and against Wednesday's close at 58.43.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 2.5 local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.4273 and 59.6077.
"We do not see much movement today because there are no signs of commercial demand. This will also keep speculators quiet," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
"But I think the rate could move up to around 58.60 to the dollar in the coming days, because we expect some import bills in the market," he added.
Dealers said low call money rates would also help the dollar to rise on demand.
Overnight call money was well supplied and the rate was quoted at 9.75 percent after opening at 10 percent, dealers said.
